## How they got there
Paris Saint-Germain secured the title by defeating Arsenal on penalties in a final that ended 1-1, with a 4-3 penalty shootout deciding the winner. Their campaign profile was defined by exceptional offensive output, as they recorded 62.6 attacks per game better than 97% of teams and executed 671 passes per game superior to all peers in their group or league phase. Additionally, the club maintained a goal difference per game of 1.25 that placed them ahead of 89% of their contemporaries during the same period.

## Would the model have picked them?
The analysis indicates that the model would not have selected Paris Saint-Germain as its top choice, noting they ranked fourth among knockout teams and remained outside its preferred top two despite being a leading contender. While the base rate suggests only an 8.3% chance for any random team to reach the final, the model assigned them a 16.1% probability of success. This statistical expectation aligns most closely with reaching the semi-finals on the model's stage scale.

## Weak spots
The club displayed no clear weak spot among its last three listed statistics, as it beat fewer than half of teams only in metrics where lower values are preferred or where performance was already high relative to the field. Specifically, they ranked 71st percentile for points per game and 56th for shot accuracy, yet these figures do not constitute a clear weakness under the criteria that requires beating fewer than half of teams on the final three stats in the list. The only stat where they beat significantly fewer than half was long passes at 8%, but this falls outside the specific "last three" constraint used to define weak spots for this report.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
